APhO-theory-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical problems only (experimental problems are not included yet). Each statement is transcribed from the official English paper of the organisers and checked part by part against its page images. Statements only: no solutions, answers or marking schemes.

ASO-Physics-problems.json.verification_notes: The Australian Science Olympiad Physics exam of Australian Science Innovations (National Qualifying Examination until about 2010, then ASOE), whose results select the students for the Australian Physics Olympiad Summer School, from which the IPhO team is chosen. Multiple-choice questions (day 1) and written questions (day 2), numbered in printed order. Statements transcribed from the official question papers and checked against their page images. Statements only: no answers, marking schemes or solutions. Problems © Australian Science Innovations.

BPhO-R2-problems.json.verification_notes: Round 2 of the British Physics Olympiad (BPhO), the selection paper for the UK IPhO team, dated by the year printed on the paper (sat in January from 2011). Questions numbered as printed. Statements transcribed from the official BPhO papers and checked against their page images. Statements only: no mark schemes or solutions. Problems © British Physics Olympiad.

CAP-problems.json.verification_notes: The Canadian Association of Physicists High School/CEGEP Prize Exam, written by the Canadian Physics Olympiad (UBC); its results select the students invited to the national training camp from which the Canadian IPhO team is chosen. Section A: multiple-choice questions; Section B: long problems; numbered as printed. Statements transcribed from the official English papers and checked against their page images. Statements only: no answers or solutions. Problems © Canadian Association of Physicists / Canadian Physics Olympiad.

CPhO-problems.json.verification_notes: Theory papers of the Chinese Physics Olympiad (全国中学生物理竞赛) of the Chinese Physical Society: the national final (决赛, paper 1) and the semifinal (复赛, paper 2); problems numbered as printed. English translation of the official Chinese papers published on the CPhO committee site (cpho.pku.edu.cn), checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions or marking schemes. Problems © Chinese Physical Society.

Cyprus-pancyprian-problems.json.verification_notes: Physics paper (subject 38) of the Pancyprian Examinations, the university entrance examinations of Cyprus, set by the Examinations Service of the Ministry of Education; one record per printed question, numbered as printed, with the part of the paper (Part A, Part B, …) as paper label. Bilingual: the Greek original as printed and a faithful English translation, both checked against the page images of the official papers published on panexams.moec.gov.cy. Statements only: no solutions; the formula sheet (τυπολόγιο) is not included. Problems © the Cyprus Ministry of Education (Examinations Service).

Czech-FO-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical problems of the national round (celostátní kolo / ústřední kolo) of category A (final year of secondary school) of the Czech Physics Olympiad (Fyzikální olympiáda) of the Central Committee of the Physics Olympiad (Ústřední komise fyzikální olympiády), dated by the year of the round (edition N is held in the school year ending in 1959 + N). Problems numbered as printed. English translation of the official Czech papers published on fyzikalniolympiada.cz (licensed CC BY 3.0 CZ), checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions. The experimental problem is not included. Problems © Ústřední komise fyzikální olympiády.

EuPhO-theory-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical problems only (experimental problems are not included yet). Each statement is transcribed from the official English paper and checked part by part against its page images. Statements only: no solutions, answers or marking schemes.

Greece-EEF-problems.json.verification_notes: National final of the Panhellenic Physics Competition for Lyceum students of the Hellenic Physical Society (Ένωση Ελλήνων Φυσικών): one paper per class, Grade 12 (Γ΄ Λυκείου, paper 1), Grade 11 (Β΄ Λυκείου, paper 2) and Grade 10 (Α΄ Λυκείου, paper 3); «Δημόκριτος» since 2025. Phase B (national final) for 2008–2015 and 2021–2024; single national paper for 2016–2019 and from 2025; for 2001–2007 the archive holds one Grade 12 paper per year with no phase printed. Grades 10 and 11 before 2020: one paper per class and year with no phase printed (in 2008–2015 sat on the date of the Grade 12 Phase A); treated as the national paper of that class. Where the archive holds only a first-round paper for a class and year (e.g. Grade 12 in 2018 and 2020), that paper is not included. Problems numbered as printed, including the data-analysis problem printed in the paper. English translation of the official Greek papers, checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions. Problems © Ένωση Ελλήνων Φυσικών.

Greece-panhellenic-problems.json.verification_notes: Physics paper of the Panhellenic Examinations, the university entrance examinations of Greece, for day and evening General Lyceums (June session), set by the Ministry of Education: Φυσική Προσανατολισμού (from 2016) and Φυσική Θετικής και Τεχνολογικής Κατεύθυνσης (until 2015). One record per printed topic (ΘΕΜΑ Α, Β, Γ, Δ, numbered 1–4) with all its sub-questions. Bilingual: the Greek original as printed and a faithful English translation, both checked against the page images of the official papers published on minedu.gov.gr. Statements only: no solutions or answers. Problems © the Greek Ministry of Education.

INPhO-problems.json.verification_notes: The Indian National Physics Olympiad (INPhO) of HBCSE (Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education, TIFR), the theory paper whose results select the students for the Indian IPhO orientation-cum-selection camp (in 2021–2022 held as IOQP Part II). Questions numbered as printed. Statements transcribed from the official English papers and checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions. Problems © HBCSE.

IPhO-theory-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical problems (paper 1) and experimental problems (paper 2, the written tasks of the experimental exam: apparatus, procedure and questions; the measurements themselves need the apparatus). Each statement is transcribed from the official English paper and checked part by part against its page images; for the early years without an official English paper the source is the IPhO compilation and is labelled as such. Statements only: no solutions, answers or marking schemes.

IZhO-Physics-theory-problems.json.verification_notes: Physics theoretical competition of the International Zhautykov Olympiad in natural sciences, held every January in Almaty (Kazakhstan); one record per printed problem with all its parts and points, numbered as printed. Transcribed from the English theory papers as mirrored on olimpicos.net (the official site izho.kz was not reachable) and checked against their page images. Experimental problems are not included. Statements only: no solutions or answers. Problems © the IZhO organisers (Republican Physics and Mathematics School, Almaty).

India-JEE-Advanced-Physics-problems.json.verification_notes: Physics part of Paper 1 and Paper 2 of the Joint Entrance Examination (Advanced), the entrance examination of the Indian Institutes of Technology, dated by the year of the examination; one record per question, numbered 1..N within the Physics part of each paper (the printed question number is kept in the source check). Statements transcribed from the official English question papers published on jeeadv.ac.in (past question papers) and checked against their page images; multiple-choice options are kept, answers and answer keys are not. Problems © the Indian Institutes of Technology (JEE Advanced).

JPhO-problems.json.verification_notes: Theory paper of the Second Challenge (第2チャレンジ, the national final) of the Physics Challenge (全国物理コンテスト 物理チャレンジ) of the Japan Physics Olympiad Committee (JPhO), dated by the year of the contest; problems numbered as printed. English translation of the official Japanese papers published on jpho.jp, checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions. The experimental paper and the First Challenge are not included. Problems © JPhO (物理オリンピック日本委員会).

NBPhO-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical problems of the Nordic-Baltic Physics Olympiad (formerly the Estonian-Finnish Olympiad), numbered as printed; experimental problems are not included. Statements transcribed from the organisers' papers and checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions.

Netherlands-NNO-problems.json.verification_notes: Theory tests of the final round (eindronde / finale) of the Dutch National Physics Olympiad (Nationale Natuurkunde Olympiade) of the Stichting Natuurkunde Olympiade Nederland; problems numbered 1..N per year through the theory tests (deel 1, deel 2 / Toets 1, Toets 2, given as paper label). English translation of the official Dutch papers published on natuurkundeolympiade.nl, checked against their page images; the Dutch original is shown too. Statements only: no solutions. The practical test is not included. Problems © Stichting Natuurkunde Olympiade Nederland.

OPhO-problems.json.verification_notes: Online Physics Olympiad, an international team competition held online since 2020: the Open round (many short problems, paper 1) and the theoretical part of the Invitational round (long problems, paper 2), numbered as printed. Transcribed from the official PDFs in the archive of opho.physoly.tech and checked against their page images (2022 Open: statements taken from the official solutions PDF, the only published version). Experimental questions are not included. Statements only: no solutions or answers. Problems © Online Physics Olympiad.

PLANCKS-problems.json.verification_notes: The international final of PLANCKS, the theoretical physics competition for undergraduate and master students organised by the International Association of Physics Students (IAPS). Statements transcribed from the exam papers published by the organisers (archive of the Institute of Physics, plancks.uk) and checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions.

Physics-Cup-problems.json.verification_notes: Physics Cup, the online physics competition for secondary-school students founded by Jaan Kalda (Estonia): one hard problem at a time, posted online; hints are published weekly and reduce the score. Problems as first published, without hints: the organisers' PDFs for 2013 (WoPhO selection round, printed as Problems 6–10) and 2017–2019, and the official problem pages on physicscup.ee for 2020–2026 (2020 includes a warm-up Problem 0). The 2012 edition (IPhO 2012 Physics Cup) is not included: its site is no longer online. Statements only: no hints, solutions or answers. Problems © Physics Cup / the problem authors.

Poland-OF-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical part of the final stage (zawody III stopnia, część teoretyczna) of the Polish Physics Olympiad (Olimpiada Fizyczna) of the Komitet Główny Olimpiady Fizycznej, dated by the year of the final (edition N is held in the school year ending in 1951 + N; no final in 2020). Problems numbered as printed. English translation of the official Polish papers published on kgof.edu.pl, checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions. The experimental part is not included. Problems © Komitet Główny Olimpiady Fizycznej.

Romania-ONF-problems.json.verification_notes: National stage (etapa națională) of the Romanian National Physics Olympiad, theoretical paper (proba teoretică): one paper per grade, Grade IX (paper 1), X (paper 2), XI (paper 3) and XII (paper 4), problems numbered as printed. Bilingual: the Romanian original and a faithful English translation, both checked against the page images of the official subject papers as published in the olympiad archive olimpiade.ro. Years 2003–2019 and 2022–2025; the Grade IX papers of 2011 and 2012 are not in the archive, and the 2024 Grade XI file holds only Subiectul III. Practical (experimental) papers are not included. Statements only: no solutions or marking schemes. Problems © Ministerul Educației (Olimpiada Națională de Fizică).

Russia-VOS-problems.json.verification_notes: Theoretical round of the final stage (заключительный этап) of the All-Russian Olympiad in Physics (Всероссийская олимпиада школьников по физике), dated by the year of the spring final: one paper per grade, grade 11 (paper 1), grade 10 (paper 2) and grade 9 (paper 3). Problems numbered as printed. English translation of the official Russian papers (as published on vos.olimpiada.ru), checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions or marking criteria. Experimental rounds are not included.

Slovakia-FO-problems.json.verification_notes: National round (celoštátne kolo) of category A of the Slovak Physics Olympiad, theoretical problems, numbered as printed; year = the end of the school year (63rd FO 2021/2022 = 2022). Only the papers published by NIVAM (the organiser) are included: 2022, 2024 and 2025. Bilingual: the Slovak original and a faithful English translation, both checked against the page images of the official papers. Statements only: no solutions. Problems © NIVAM / Slovenská komisia fyzikálnej olympiády.

UK-Oxford-PAT-problems.json.verification_notes: The Physics Aptitude Test (PAT) of the University of Oxford, the admissions test for Physics and Physics & Philosophy, dated by the year in which it was sat (autumn, for entry the following year); one record per printed question, numbered as printed. Statements transcribed from the official papers published by the Department of Physics (physics.ox.ac.uk, PAT past papers, 2006–2023) and checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions. From 2024 the test was online only and its papers are not published; from 2025 the ESAT replaced the PAT. Problems © the University of Oxford.

USAPhO-problems.json.verification_notes: The USAPhO exam of the American Association of Physics Teachers (AAPT), Parts A and B, numbered per part as printed (A1–A3 → Part A 1–3). Statements transcribed from the official AAPT exam PDFs and checked against their page images. Statements only: no solutions or answers. Problems © AAPT.
